one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08 (a Sunday, so the last close is Fri Nov 6). Main event: Paycom's Q3 2026 results. They have not been announced as of Oct 11 (a search found no notice), but last year the notice came Oct 16, 2025 for results after the close on Nov 5, 2025 [25], so a print inside the window is likely (~85%), not certain. Earnings reactions are large: Aug 6, 2026 was +23.55% (close $174.80 to $215.97) [5]. Expectations are higher now: the stock is at 17.7x forward EPS, near the 17.09x HCM peer median [4,17-24], and $12 under the 52-week high, so I see no reason to lean either way on the print. Industry read-across inside the window: ADP reports fiscal Q1 before the open on Oct 28 [16] (pays-per-control and retention read). Paychex already said Management Solutions came in slightly below plan, in a 'low fire, low hire' market [8]. The FOMC meets Oct 27-28 [15], after a September hike [14]; a hold or hike is a small float-income tailwind against Paycom's ~$105M guide [2]. September payrolls were weak (+29K, -60K revisions) [11], but small-business indices are steady [12,13]. The founder's 10b5-1 sales cannot start before Dec 1, 2026 [26], so they fall outside the window. Round 1 tilted the centre +0.5% on estimate-revision momentum from a key-gated feed; that is dropped. Net: a symmetric lognormal with median at spot $232.22 and sigma 0.14 (vs 46%/3.5 = 13.1%), widened slightly for the likely earnings gap.

fair_value.method: Blend of a 12-month-forward P/E (70%: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of $15.13 x 16.5x = $249.6) and TTM EV/EBITDA at the horizon (30%: est. TTM EBITDA $808.6M x 14.5x = EV $11.72B, less $784.8M lease-inclusive net debt, / 43.27M shares = $252.8). Multiples sit inside the 8-name HCM/payroll/PEO peer range (median fwd P/E 17.09x, TTM EV/EBITDA 15.2x). Base share count corrected to the 10-Q's 45.07M.

inputs_detail.derivation: S&P Global consensus shown on StockAnalysis; +15.45% on FY26 $12.10

Revenue +6.5%: below FY27 consensus +7.44% [3] because FY26 guide +7-8% vs Q2 +9.8% implies H2 deceleration [2], ADP guides FY27 revenue +5-6% with pays per control 0-1% [7], Paylocity's FY27 guide is +6.2% to +7.0% ($1.880-1.895B on $1.771B) [9], payrolls +29K [11], small-business jobs index flat [12]. Margin: ~+2% EPS from operating leverage (Q2 adj. EBITDA margin 44% [2]; FY26 guide ~46% [2]). Share count: ~-4% average (see buyback derivation in the EV/EBITDA method: ~$432M/yr of buybacks from normalized FCF [1,4]). 1.065 x 1.02 / 0.96 = 1.132, i.e. +13%; I cut it to +11% because interest on the $900M drawn [1] (Q2 interest expense $10.5M [1], ~$42M/yr) does not shrink when debt is not repaid, and because of flat-employment risk to per-employee revenue.
One quarter of FY27 and three of FY28 remain at the horizon: 0.25 x $13.97 + 0.75 x $15.51 = $3.49 + $11.63 = $15.13 (round 1 applied the multiple to full FY28 EPS, which overstated the NTM base)

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: TTM EBITDA $735.1M x 1.10 = $808.6M at horizon; x 14.5x TTM EV/EBITDA = EV $11,725M; less net debt $784.8M (lease-inclusive, same basis as the EV) = $10,940M equity; / 43.27M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis EBITDA (TTM), the same basis as the peer EV/EBITDA figures [citation gate 2026-10-12: the page shows $735.1M, but it is StockAnalysis's own EBITDA definition, not a figure Paycom reports, so 'reported' is a mislabel. Filings-derived TTM GAAP EBITDA is $844.0M (operating income 567.2 - 297.5 + 378.7 = $648.4M + D&A 176.3 - 81.9 + 101.2 = $195.6M; FY25 8-K Ex.99.1, 10-Q R4/R7). Agent value unchanged; the reconciled numbers no longer use it.]

$735.1M x 1.10. The horizon TTM window runs about 5 quarters ahead of today's: ~7% revenue growth per year [3] x 1.25 years = ~9%, plus a little margin expansion (Q2 adj. EBITDA margin 44%, FY26 guide ~46% [2]), less H2 deceleration [2]

Peer median TTM EV/EBITDA is 15.2x ((13.47 + 16.92)/2; range 11.99x INTU to 63.71x NSP) [17-24]. PAYC is at 15.06x on StockAnalysis EV [4], or ~15.3x on 45.07M shares ($232.22 x 45.07M = $10,466M + $784.8M = $11,251M / $735.1M). I use 14.5x, ~5% below the median, for the same reasons as the P/E discount. Round 1's derived 'forward' multiple (TTM / (1 + 3Y revenue CAGR)) is dropped; reported TTM multiples are used instead. [citation gate 2026-10-12: TTM EV/EBITDA figures are StockAnalysis aggregator ratios and were not rebuilt from filings; no reconciled number uses them.]

Jun 30, 2026: $900.0M long-term debt + $28.8M + $54.0M operating lease liabilities - $198.0M cash = $784.8M [1]; matches StockAnalysis [4]. Lease-inclusive to match the EV in the EBITDA multiple. Held flat to the horizon because all normalized FCF is assumed to go to dividends and buybacks (no FCF is credited to both shares and net debt).
10-Q cover: 45,071,619 at Jul 28, 2026, including 786,338 restricted shares (round 1 used 44.29M, which excludes restricted stock)
TTM FCF $575.1M [4] includes a one-off +$74.8M 'income taxes, net' inflow in H1-2026 OCF [1]: $575.1M - $74.8M = $500.3M

$500.3M FCF - dividends $1.50 x 45.07M = $67.6M [4,1] = $432.7M. That is well inside the $2.0B no-expiry plan approved May 4, 2026 [6]: at least $1.65B is left even if all $349.0M of Q2 repurchases [1] fell under the new plan
$432.7M / ~$240 average price = 1.80M shares = 4.0% of 45.07M: 45.07M x 0.96 = 43.27M. SBC dilution (H1 SBC $31.6M [1]) is treated as offset by the restricted shares already in the count

bear.story: Employment turns negative (payrolls already +29K with -60K revisions [11]; ADP guides pays per control 0-1% [7]; Paychex sees 'low fire, low hire' [8]). Paycom's first FY27 guide (Feb 2027) comes in below the $2.37B / $13.97 consensus [3], and H2-2026 deceleration [2] continues to ~4-5% revenue growth. NTM EPS at the horizon ~$13.6 x 12.5x (just under the lowest HCM peer, INTU 12.64x [21]) = ~$170. Founder 10b5-1 selling of up to 1.09M shares (~2.4% of 45.07M) Dec 2026-Jun 2027 adds supply [26].

base.story: Revenue ~6.5-7%, in line with the industry (ADP +5-6% [7], Paylocity FY27 guide ~+6.6% at the midpoint [9]). Margins edge up, buybacks from ~$500M normalized FCF shrink shares ~4% a year [1,4,6], and float income runs slightly above guide after the Sep hike [14]. NTM EPS ~$15.1 x ~16.4x (just under the 17.09x peer median [17-24]) = ~$248.

bull.story: The FY27 guide surprises up, with revenue at 9-10% as in Q2 (+9.8%, recurring +11.0% [2]), adj. EBITDA margin above 47%, and a faster buyback under the $2.0B no-expiry plan [6] (H1-2026 pace was $1.42B [1]). NTM EPS ~$16.4 x ~19.2x (between PCTY 17.61x and ADP 22.09x [17,19]) = ~$315. A sector takeout bid is possible (Dayforce went private [27]). Prediction-market Fed odds were removed from this case.

A sustained trade there would mean the market has thrown out the Q2 re-rating: FY27 numbers are breaking (bookings or retention failing, employment contraction hitting per-employee revenue, or buybacks paused under the $2.0B plan [6]), which is more than ordinary 46%-vol noise. Moved from $165 to $162 because the verified pre-print closes ($163.96-$174.80) replace the round-1 weekly low that came from a key-gated feed.

reasoning: Lane: industry/value chain. Round-2 changes follow the supervisor's checks, each confirmed at source. (a) Shares: 45.07M per the 10-Q cover, which includes 786,338 restricted shares [1]. (b) Consensus: FY27 EPS $13.97 from S&P Global via StockAnalysis [3] replaces the key-gated Alpha Vantage $13.95, and the AV revision statistics are dropped. (c) FCF: the H1 OCF includes a +$74.8M one-off tax inflow [1], so normalized FCF is ~$500M (TTM $575.1M [4] less $74.8M); buybacks are ~$432M/yr after dividends, i.e. ~4% of shares a year, not 5%. (d) Buyback plan: $2.0B, no expiry, approved May 4, 2026 [6]. (e) Comps: XRO, BILL, SGE.L and ASUR are dropped, leaving 8 HCM/payroll/PEO names [17-24] (median fwd P/E 17.09x, TTM EV/EBITDA 15.2x). The derived forward EV/EBITDA is replaced by reported TTM multiples, and that method's weight is cut from 40% to 30%. (f) Paylocity's guide now comes from its own release [9], not an AI summary. Rippling's vendor survey and the prediction-market Fed odds are removed from every number. (g) Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage URLs (key-gated) are replaced by StockAnalysis price history [5]. Industry read: volume growth from employment is ~0-1% (ADP pays per control 0-1% [7], Paychex flat employment and 'low fire, low hire' [8], BLS +29K [11], small-business jobs index 99.15 [12], ADP NER small establishments +23K [13]). Vendors therefore grow on price, attach and share. Paylocity guides +6.2% to +7.0% [9], ADP +5-6% [7], and Workday HCM subscription +13.9% [10] shows upmarket demand is healthy. Paycom's Q2 +9.8% [2] is top of the SMB/mid-market group, but its own guide implies ~6% in H2. Valuation: NTM EPS at the horizon is $15.13 (FY27 $13.97 [3]; FY28E +11%). At 16.5x that gives $249.6; the TTM EV/EBITDA leg gives $252.8; the 70/30 blend is $250.6, +8% vs $232.22 (round 1: $260.7). Distribution: a three-scenario lognormal mixture (bear $170/25%, base $248/50%, bull $315/25%, within-scenario sigma 0.24), median ~$243, 10th-90th percentile ~$155-$362 (effective vol ~33%). That is below the 46% trailing realized, which included both a guide crash and a +23.55% re-rating day [5], but above a typical large-cap because four prints, including the FY27 guide, fall inside the horizon. P(>= $232) = 0.554. Research limits: sec.gov refused a generic curl client and StockAnalysis returned a bot-protection challenge to curl, so both were read with WebFetch. The Paycom prepared-remarks PDF was not machine-readable, so the $1.66B remaining authorization is not used; only the lower bound ($2.0B less at most $349.0M of Q2 repurchases) is. FY28 consensus is paywalled. No option data was consulted.
